- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (especially > -0.4) — model tends to ignore downside risk.
- Underestimate sharp downward moves after recent spikes — model fails to capture momentum reversal.
- Overshoot early in forecast horizon when sentiment is mildly positive — model overreacts to short-term optimism.
- Mean-reversion bias: model holds prices too high in the middle of forecast horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Lagged correction: model often underreacts to sentiment shifts occurring 2–3 days prior — adjust forecast by 0.5–1.0% downward if sentiment turns negative within 3 days.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day forecasts — especially when sentiment is volatile or recent lows are below 65 — reduce forecast by 1–2% for each 0.10 drop in sentiment average over last 7 days.
